record.original_question: Can one construct trial-function and test-function families for Petrov-Galerkin or related spectral methods that are not tailored to only one specific fractional differential equation but instead work across a broad class of problems, still guarantee rapid convergence, possibly yield even faster convergence than current constructions, and admit error analyses in stronger norms such as L^infinity rather than only L^2?

evidence.quote: From a practical perspective, it would be advantageous to have a set of test functions and a set of trial functions that could be used not just for one type of differential equations but for a broad class of such problems.

The search for sets of such basis functions (that, of course, should be able to guarantee a rapid convergence of the sequence of approximate solutions towards the exact solution) is a topic of great interest.
Moreover, one might raise the question whether a different construction of the basis and test functions could lead to an even faster convergence.

A notable weakness of this approach that might also be addressed in future research projects is that one is naturally lead to consider the covergence behaviour and the error estimates in an L2 norm only whereas other solvers for fractional ordinary differential equations are usually analyzed with respect to the stronger Linfinity norm.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider linear fractional differential equations on a bounded interval, for instance equations of the form
   D^α u(x) + L u(x) = f(x),   x ∈ (a,b),
together with appropriate initial or boundary conditions, where D^α denotes a Caputo or Riemann–Liouville fractional derivative of order α ∈ (0,1) ∪ (1,2) and L is a (possibly zero) lower-order linear operator. For such problems, a Petrov–Galerkin spectral method seeks an approximation u_N in a finite-dimensional trial space span{φ_1,…,φ_N} by imposing the weak orthogonality conditions
   ⟨D^α u_N + L u_N − f, ψ_k⟩ = 0,   k = 1,…,N,
against a finite-dimensional test space span{ψ_1,…,ψ_N}.

Construct an explicit pair of families {φ_n}_{n≥1} and {ψ_n}_{n≥1} of trial and test functions with the following properties simultaneously:

1. (Universality) The same families work for a broad class of fractional differential equations — at minimum, for all sufficiently smooth right-hand sides f and for a non-trivial range of fractional orders α and of admissible lower-order operators L — rather than being tailored to a single equation.

2. (Rapid convergence) For sufficiently regular exact solutions u, the approximations u_N converge to u at a spectral (faster than any algebraic) rate; ideally at a rate at least as fast as that achieved by existing equation-specific constructions, and if possible strictly faster.

3. (Strong-norm error analysis) The convergence and error estimates can be established in the L^∞(a,b) norm, i.e. one can prove bounds of the form
   ‖u − u_N‖_{L^∞(a,b)} ≤ C(u) η(N),   η(N) → 0 rapidly,
and not merely in the L^2(a,b) norm.

Either exhibit such families together with proofs of (1)–(3), or prove that no families satisfying all three properties simultaneously can exist.
artifact.category_tag: Spectral methods for fractional differential equations
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open research direction concerning the construction of universal trial/test bases for Petrov–Galerkin spectral discretizations of fractional ODEs with L^∞ error analysis. No published work appears to provide such a construction with all three properties (universality across a broad class, provable spectral convergence, and L^∞ error estimates); standard treatments (e.g., Jacobi poly-fractonomial bases of Zayernouri–Karniadakis and subsequent developments) are analyzed in weighted L^2 settings and are largely problem-specific. Status remains open to the best of available evidence.

status_evidence.title: Fractional Sturm–Liouville eigen-problems: Theory and numerical approximation
status_evidence.snippet: Poly-fractonomial bases for spectral approximation of fractional problems, with weighted L^2 analysis.
status_evidence.claim: Existing Petrov–Galerkin fractional spectral bases are analyzed in L^2-type norms and tailored to specific operators.
